issues.description: mutations.ts is 656 lines — a large single module (mandated as one file by the packet; cohesive but unsplit).

updateDummyOutlet persists only `name` into the store graph; category/city/district/address/is_active are echoed in the return value but not written back, so a subsequent read does not reflect them (outlet mutation is not a T11 DELIVERABLE GWT, so non-blocking).

Promotion mutators write to graph.promotions, but the promotions read path (listDummyPromotions) derives the list independently from products and ignores graph.promotions, so created/updated/deleted promotions do not surface in the list (pre-existing T9 read-path design; not a T11 GWT).

strengths: Merge resolution is faithful: every T8/T9/T10 read guard (withDummyRead / useDummyRefresh / extracted loaders) coexists with every T11 write guard in the same file; the 10 write guards are wired to the correct dummy mutators (updateDummyOutlet, updateDummyProductPrice, 4 promotion mutators, assignDummyUserRole, createDummyOrder, updateDummyDelivery, createDummyPayment, createDummyOutletOrder, createDummyVisit, sendDummyFunnelEvent).
No conflict markers, no duplicate function definitions, and no orphaned imports in any of the 12 touched files.
Pure mutator + store-bound wrapper separation keeps mutators independently testable; mutations.ts never imports the API layer, avoiding runtime cycles.
ID-collision safety implemented via `dummy-` string prefix, negative numeric ids, and `nextDummyNumericId` scanning across all numeric-key collections.
1:1 relational side-effects (order -> payment + invoice + delivery) applied from BOTH order entry points (createSalesOrder and OrderForm).
Single cross-writes zero-fetch integration assertion covers all 10 write paths, plus OFF-path regression and toggle-cycle ephemerality.
